name: Ironpass DeepStrata Tunneling Suit Pro
description:
Gunmetal grey reinforced with rust-orange abrasion panels across the knees, elbows, and shoulder caps. The DeepStrata is a purpose-built tunneling suit for underground excavation in M88's subsurface infrastructure corridors — where collapses, gas pockets, and groundwater intrusion are occupational hazards rather than emergencies. Shell is ripstop ballistic nylon over a crushproof foam chassis at impact zones.

Integrated kneepads are gel-filled with a hard outer cap. The collar accepts a standard tunnel respirator bayonet mount. Spinal channel runs full-length up the back, accommodating spinal rigs and exoskeletal harness attachments. Pockets are sealed with magnetic closures rated for dust ingress.
functionality: Impact protection at knees, elbows, and shoulders; spinal channel accommodates spinal rigs and exoskeletal harness mounts; collar bayonet mount accepts standard tunnel respirators; magnetic-seal pockets rated IP65 for dust; reinforced seat panel for confined-space crawl work.
what_it_says: You work below the city where no one is watching and everything can go wrong.
story_hooks: A tunnel crew breaks through a sealed pre-collapse corridor and finds it occupied — someone has been living in the deep grid for years, and they've built something down there.
The spinal channel was spec'd to accommodate standard rigs, but a new military-grade spinal augment doesn't fit — its owner needs a modified suit before the next shift or can't work.
A tunnel worker's suit data-logger — used for safety compliance — has been recording audio; a labor organizer wants the files before the corponation's safety inspector does.
